To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
metallomacrocyles composed of naphthalene dihydroxamic acid ligands and Cu2+ metal ions have liquid crystallinity depending on the length and structure of their side chains.

metallomacrocyclic liquid crystals were synthesized by the self-assembly of naphthalene-dihydroxamate ligands and Cu2+ions, and the crystallinity and liquid-crystallinity of the macrocyclic complexes depend on the structure and length of the peripheral alkoyl chains, with the oligo(ethylene)glycol side chains being particularly effective in inducing the formation of an ordered lamellar mesophase.

metallomacrocyles composed of naphthalene-based dihydroxamic acid and copper(II) ions were successfully synthesized through a 1:1 self-assembly, and the crystallinity and liquid crystal property of the macrocycles were sharply dependent on the length and structure of peripheral alkyl chains, and that the metallomacrocycle composed of oligo(ethylene) glycol side chains exhibited liquid crystalline property.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the self-assembled synthesis of macrocycles and their liquid crystalline properties.
the synthesis and liquid crystalline property of metallomacromolecules, which is a promising approach to the design and synthesis of novel liquid crystal materials with unique functions.
the synthesis of a series of metallodendritic compounds and their liquid crystallinity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the metallomacrocycle can be a promising candidate for LC materials.

the LC properties of the metallomacrocycle are determined by the balance of the intermolecular interactions between macrocycles, such as π-π, hydrogen bonding, and van der Waals forces, and the flexibility of the macrocyclic structure.
the self-assembled metallomacrocyclic structure can be controlled by peripheral alkyl chains and the LC property can be tuned by oligo(ethylene) glycol side chains.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the self-assembled metallomacrocycle can be a useful platform for the construction of a variety of LC materials.
the metallomacromolecular assembly can be controlled by the combination of the macrocycle structure and the included metal ions.
the self-assembled macrocycle can form a liquid crystalline phase by introducing appropriate side chains, which is a new type of liquid crystal that can be used in various fields.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the metallomacroligand with the proper peripheral chains can be used as the building block to construct LCs with a variety of mesophases.
the metallomacrocycle is a useful platform to control the self-assembly of included molecules in a flowable LC phase.
the self-assembly of metallomacromolecules is a useful method to control the molecular packing of macrocycles.
